source._php_version_note: Drupal 11.4.11 requires PHP >= 8.3.0 (core/lib/Drupal.php MINIMUM_PHP; drupal/core composer.json php >=8.3.0) and recommends 8.4. The image runs Ubuntu 24.04's own PHP 8.3 (8.3.6 with Ubuntu's security backports), as wordpress, bookstack and moodle do: PHP 8.4 on Ubuntu 24.04 would need a third-party archive.
source.composer_install_cmd: composer require --no-update drupal/core-recommended:11.4.13 drupal/core-composer-scaffold:11.4.13 drupal/core-project-message:11.4.13 drupal/core-recipe-unpack:11.4.13 && composer update --no-dev --optimize-autoloader --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist && test "$(php -r "require 'vendor/autoload.php'; echo \\Drupal::VERSION;")" = 11.4.13
source._composer_note: drupal/recommended-project's composer.json asks for ^11.4 of each core package; requiring them at exactly 11.4.11 makes the resolved core the release this image is named after, and the final test fails the vendor stage otherwise. composer runs the drupal/core-composer-scaffold plugin, which writes web/index.php, web/.htaccess, web/sites/default/default.settings.php and the other scaffold files. No composer.lock is shipped by the template, so composer resolves the dependency versions at vendor time; they are frozen in the vendored tree (composer.lock and vendor/composer/installed.json are in the archive).
source._ext_note: drupal/core composer.json requires ext-date dom filter gd hash json pcre PDO session SimpleXML SPL tokenizer xml zlib; opcache and mbstring are recommended. From Ubuntu's packages: php8.3-gd, -xml (dom, simplexml, xml), -mbstring, -curl (update status and HTTP client), -zip, -sqlite3 (pdo_sqlite, the default database), -mysql (pdo_mysql), -pgsql (pdo_pgsql); opcache with php8.3-cli, the rest with php8.3-common. source.php_extensions is what the build asserts both the Apache and the CLI configuration load.
source._prune_note: Test code only, never loaded by a site (extension discovery skips tests/ directories unless extension_discovery_scan_tests is set): web/core/tests (core's PHPUnit/Nightwatch suite) and every module's, theme's and profile's tests/ directory (their test modules and fixtures). Chain 632's verdict (2026-10-22) counted 5 fixable critical/high plus 4 more from OSV in composer:drupal/core and drupal/core-recommended 9.8.0: those are core/modules/package_manager/tests/fixtures/fake_site/composer.lock and vendor/composer/installed.json, a fake Drupal 9.8.0 site Package Manager's tests stage, which scanners read as installed packages (the image's real core is 11.4.11, /opt/drupal/composer.lock). core/modules/system/tests/fixtures/HtaccessTest carries a composer.lock, package-lock.json and yarn.lock the same way. web/core/package.json and yarn.lock describe the JavaScript build toolchain of core's committed assets, not anything the site runs.
